title: test(eslint-rules): declare the RuleTester spec's own addresses as fixture data (objectui#9892)
body:
Part of objectui#9892 — the FREE file only. The other rows on that card stay open and named: six wait on objectui#9584 and three on objectui#9391, which are two different events, and that split is why the card exists in this shape.

## What this does

`eslint-rules/no-line-address-in-test-name.test.js` is a RuleTester spec. Every line address in it is fixture data — a string handed to the rule under test, or the `errors[].data.address` that has to echo what the rule extracted from that string. Four `fixture-address: REASON` declarations (the class PR objectui#9879 landed; the placeholder is spelled as a word on purpose, the literal angle-bracket form does not survive being stored here) now cover the rows the census judges false.

⛔ **No address moves.** The diff is four added comment lines plus a changeset — insertions only, zero deletions.

## Deliverable 1 — the count re-derived with the census, and it differs from the card

Measured with `scripts/cross-file-line-citation-census.mjs` itself, at base `706e09f27`. ⛔ Not an approximation of it:

| reading, for the FREE file | value |
|:--|--:|
| addresses in the census population | 26 |
| of those, judged FALSE against today's tree | 7 |
| the card's number | 5 |

⭐ **The difference is real, and its cause is measured rather than guessed.** Judging the same file's rows against the cited files **as they stood at `4b5772299`** — objectui#9879's own landing commit, whose classification pass the card inherited — returns **5**, the card's number exactly. The two extra rows today are the pair whose fixture token is the ObjectView address ending `2218`: commit `0c789a402` (objectui#9936) shifted `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx` so that line now carries a bare closing delimiter, flipping the verdict `anchor-absent` → `non-substantive`, i.e. unjudged → FALSE.

⇒ the card's 5 was a correct reading of objectui#9879's tree and is stale on today's. What made it stale is the exact defect this class exists to describe: an unrelated pull request moved lines under a stored address. The population count (26) is unchanged between the two commits — only the verdicts moved.

## The seven rows, their reasons, and why each reason survives the cited file moving

Grouped as they sit in the file: each `invalid` case is one fixture whose input token and expected-message token must stay byte-identical, so one declaration covers the pair and the census prints both rows.

1. **valid leg, the case-table `producer` field** (`app-shell/src/views/…` ObjectView address) — *RuleTester input; the rule reads this token's SHAPE, so no real address would make the case any truer.* Survives a move because it asserts nothing about the cited file: the rule's subject is the token's shape, and the case would read the same if the cited file were deleted.
2. **invalid leg, the double-quoted title flavour** (the ObjectView address ending `2218`, twice) — *RuleTester input and the expected data that must echo it; repairing either changes what this case pins.* Survives a move: the claim is about the relation between two tokens inside this file, not about where the cited line is.
3. **invalid leg, the `describe(` flavour** (the `layout.ts` address, twice) — *the parsed input and its expected message data; the rule under test reads this token, and both copies must stay equal.* Same reason shape, same immunity: it names the reader (the rule) and the equality, never a target line.
4. **invalid leg, the nested `$row.src` path** (the `packages/react/README.md` address, twice) — *the input the rule extracts from and the address it must report; one fixture, and neither names a line to find.* Survives a move because it says outright that nothing here names a line to find.

⛔ None of the four reasons mentions what is at the cited line, so none of them can be falsified by the cited file moving — which is the rot this class exists to stop one level up.

## Falsifiable zone

- **Does every declared row belong to the class?** Yes, and it is measured, not asserted: population 1272 → 1265, FALSE 600 → 593, declared 19 → 26. `resolves` (196) and unjudged (476) are **unchanged**, so all seven rows removed came out of the FALSE bucket and none out of a bucket where an address might still be a live pointer.
- **Is any of the seven genuinely repairable?** No. Six are an input/expected pair that must stay equal to each other, and the seventh is a valid-leg fixture the rule must NOT flag. In every case the address's job is to be address-shaped; there is nothing to repair it to.
- **Did any declaration over-reach onto a neighbouring row?** No. The declaration window reaches two lines, so placement was chosen to reach only the intended addresses and the census's own printed list confirms exactly seven declared rows in this file, with the nineteen others still counted.
- **Any address changed?** No — insertions only.
- **Any row outside the FREE file?** No — the diff is one test file plus one changeset.

## Deliberately NOT declared, and why

Nineteen addresses in this same file stay in the population as `no-such-file` / `ambiguous-basename` / `anchor-absent` (the synthetic ones such as the `a/b.ts` and `Foo.tsx` fixtures). They are fixture data too, but objectui#9879's own precedent is that this class was drawn over the FALSE rows: in `scripts/__tests__/check-i18n-call-site-keys.test.ts` it declared the rows that judge `non-substantive` and left the `no-such-file` rows of the very same synthetic tree undeclared. Widening the class to unjudged rows is a decision for the card that owns the class, ⛔ not for this one.

## Verification

Run through the shared verify lock:

- `pnpm exec vitest run eslint-rules/no-line-address-in-test-name.test.js scripts/__tests__/cross-file-line-citation-census.test.ts scripts/__tests__/check-new-cross-file-line-citations.test.ts` — `Test Files 3 passed (3)`, `Tests 130 passed (130)`, exit 0.
- `node scripts/cross-file-line-citation-census.mjs` — exit 0, all five declaration-reader controls plus both firing/non-firing controls PASS, so this run is a reading.
- `node scripts/check-new-cross-file-line-citations.mjs` — `VERDICT new-cross-file-line-citations: 0 new citation(s), enforcement report-only -> exit 0`; the seven rows are listed as declared, so both readers agree on one carve-out.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` — `✅ No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed.` The changeset here is therefore the empty-front-matter form that declares no release explicitly. ⛔ No `skip-changeset` label is applied: in this repo that label is read by nothing.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test …` — `NOT GOVERNED`, both paths.
- `pnpm exec eslint` on both changed paths — exit 0.

⚠️ A red `Test (shard n/4)` job on this PR is very unlikely to be this diff: those jobs run within seconds of their twenty-minute ceiling and have been measured cancelling and succeeding on the same commit. objectui#9584 is the repair for that and it is waiting on a human.
